In upstream proxy mode, the CONNECT sent to the upstream proxy now brackets an IPv6 literal target, so it goes out as `CONNECT [::1]:443` instead of `CONNECT ::1:443`. I did not add a test and did not run anything.

The change is in `HttpUpstreamProxy.start_handshake` in `mitmproxy/proxy/layers/http/_upstream_proxy.py`. If the IDNA-encoded host contains a `:`, it is wrapped in `[...]` before the port is appended. Domain names and IPv4 addresses come out as before.

Because `authority` is reused for the optional `Host` header (`http_connect_send_host_header`), that header is bracketed too, which is what RFC 7230 requires for IPv6 hosts.

The existing `test_upstream_proxy` in `test/mitmproxy/proxy/layers/http/test_http.py` could be extended with an IPv6 case, but its parametrization is intricate, so I left it alone.
